title: USB drives and chargers in practice
intro: A found flash drive is no gift. Decide what you would do in each moment from this module's lessons.

decisions.title: Message from +994 51 000 77 63
decisions.prompt: A flash drive is lying on your desk. What do you do with this message?

body: Hello, I'm Nigar, the director's new assistant.
We left a flash drive on your desk, it's the director's presentation.
Please plug it in and open the file now, the meeting starts in 10 minutes. Don't tell anyone yet.

options.label: Plug it in and open the file
Call the director's office on the number I know
Reply and ask which file to open

decisions.explain: An unknown number, the director's name, time pressure and secrecy. Check through a channel you already know.

decisions.title: Salaries_2026_confidential.xlsx
decisions.prompt: This drive was lying in the car park. What do you do with this file?

artifact.name: Salaries_2026_confidential.xlsx
artifact.text: Source: USB drive found in the car park

options.label: Plug it into my work computer and open it
Check it on my home computer
Take the drive to the security team

decisions.explain: Plugging it in can be enough: some devices pretend to be a keyboard and type commands by themselves.

decisions.title: Message from Kamal (colleague)
decisions.prompt: A colleague offers to look at the drive for you. What do you do with this message?

artifact.name: Kamal (colleague)
body: Give it to me, I'll look. I have antivirus on my computer.

options.label: Hand it over, the antivirus will protect him
Politely refuse and hand it in

decisions.explain: Antivirus does not stop a device that types commands. Security checks drives on a computer isolated from the network.

decisions.title: Trust this computer?
decisions.prompt: Your phone is charging from a cable a stranger lent you at the airport. What do you do?

artifact.title: Trust this computer?
body: Your settings and data will be accessible from this computer when connected.

options.label: Don't trust, and unplug the cable

decisions.explain: A charging cable should never ask for trust. Charge with your own adapter from a wall socket or your own power bank.
